newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shares follow indecisive pattern.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shares follow indecisive pattern.

text.p: Cyprus shares fell by 1.22 percent by the week's end on Friday as the market followed an indecisive pattern sparked by optimistic and pessimistic views expressed on the outlook of the economy, analysts said.

"The Cyprus stock market followed a yo-yo pattern during February... views expressed on the prospects of the economy vary from "good" to "not so good" in case the tension on the political issue does not completely defuse soon," CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation said in its weekly market review.

Businessmen have blamed the slowdown to an extent on "artificial" tension created early last month after disclosures Cyprus is buying an anti-aircraft system from Russia, and warnings from Turkey it would block the deployment.
Turkey invaded the northern third of the island in 1974 in response to a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military junta ruling Greece.
"Politics is the main force affecting the market at the moment," said one trader with Laiki Investments.
The Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index, set at 100 points, closed at 76.05 during Friday's trading from 76.99 last week.
Analysts have put the PE ratio of the market at around 16.
Banking stocks, traditionally the strongest sector of the 40-share market, closed at 87.37 points from 87.73 last week.
The closing price for Bank of Cyprus fully paid shares was down two cents from last week, at 325.5.

Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank, were trading at 314, down two cents from last week. Earlier Friday the bank announced its 1996 pre-tax profit was up 6.2 percent to 27.641 million pounds ($54.5 million) after a 17.5 percent increase the previous year.

The Hellenic Bank dropped half a cent and was trading at 266.5. The bank's board of directors is due to examine its 1996 results on March 5. The Universal Savings Bank dropped 2.5 cents to 165 on its fully paid shares.
Universal Life Insurance shares were trading at 402.5, unchanged from last week, and Paneuropean was down three cents, trading at 104.5.

Cement producer Vassiliko was trading at 137.5 from 138.5 last week and beer and wine manufacturers Keo dropped 5.5 cents. Shares of national carrier Cyprus Airways were trading for 29 cents from 30 last week.
